TerrainBlock.why: The walk stopped at the guarded call ending TerrainBlock::unpackUpdate (0x59ac6a) having judged it to read nothing, so the layout was short by the material-name list: 1219 bits against the 1735 a recorded session carries. Cross-checking against t2-demo-parser (MIT, github.com/exogen/t2-demo-parser), which decodes the same function by hand, named the missing tail -- a flag and then one string holding the eight material names joined by newlines. The two sections before it, the init mask and the empty-square runs, are written out here as well: the walked graph reached them by two duplicated paths, and one clean pair is easier to check against terrData.cc than a graph that says the same thing twice.
TerrainBlock.assumes: The material-name flag is read unconditionally. Tribes 2 reads it only when the connection's protocol version is above 51, which build 25034 is; a server older than that would need the version threading through to the layout.

Precipitation.why: The walk read 243 bits on one session and 339 on another where both carry 379: its graph takes a short path through the four mask flags. Written out here from the same function the walk reads (0x681260), with the field order cross-checked against t2-demo-parser (MIT, github.com/exogen/t2-demo-parser), which notes the binary's mask order is InitMask, StormShowMask, StormMask, PercentageMask -- not the order the published V12 source has.

Player.why: ShapeBase reads a flag per mounted image slot only when the object is not yet in the scene, so one graph of the bits cannot describe both an initial body and an update -- the walk in ghostwalk.py read 126 to 166 bits where a session carries 276 to 351.  Written out from the retail binary's own reading (0x5db2d0), with the field order cross-checked against t2-demo-parser (MIT, github.com/exogen/t2-demo-parser), and measured against recorded sessions by Tools/t2/xcdiff.py.

Sky.why: The walk read Sky's three cloud layers as a counted loop and took the count off the wire, so the layout treated a thirty-two bit field as a repeat count and lost the rest of the packet -- which lost four guaranteed events with it and stalled the ordered queue.  The layers are a loop of exactly three; the wire count belongs to the fog volumes, several fields earlier.  Written out from 0x5ab580 and cross-checked against t2-demo-parser.

Vehicle.why: The walk explores past four and a half million states and comes back with a cycle in it, so there was no layout for this class at all.  Written out from the retail binary's own reading (0x60d740), cross-checked against t2-demo-parser (MIT, github.com/exogen/t2-demo-parser).  Shares shape_base(), which carries the initial-only image flag.
